title: Input Tag
body:
`<input>` — the general-purpose form control. A void element whose behaviour is set by its `type`.

```html
<input type="text" name="email" placeholder="you@example.com">
<input type="password" name="pw">
<input type="checkbox" name="subscribe" checked>
<input type="submit" value="Send">
```

The `name` attribute is what matters on submission: it becomes the key in the submitted data, so an input without a `name` is simply not sent. `value` holds the current contents, and reading `input.value` from [[JavaScript]] is the normal way to get at what the user typed.

Type-based validation (`type="email"`, `required`, `min`, `max`) is a convenience for the user, not a security control — it runs on the [[Client]] and can be bypassed trivially, so the server must validate everything again. Usually lives inside a [[Form Tag]]. See [[HTML]].
